svg.text: Linux USB hotplug: from plug-in to a working device
A USB device whose driver exists on the system, attached to an xHCI host controller. Example IDs are a Logitech receiver (046d:c52b) handled by usbhid → input.
VBUS 5 V powers the device (≤100 mA until configured)
Device pulls up D+ (full/high speed) or D− (low speed)
Hub sets the port's C_PORT_CONNECTION status bit
USB 3: SuperSpeed link training (LFPS, Polling → U0)
External hub: bitmap on its interrupt-IN endpoint
Root hub: xHCI puts a Port Status Change Event
on the event ring and raises an MSI-X interrupt
Hub drives SE0 on the port for 10–20 ms
Device enters Default state, answers address 0
Speed read from port status: LS / FS / HS / SS
Device answers SETUP packets on the default pipe
xHCI Enable Slot command → slot ID
Endpoints live; may now draw bMaxPower
xHCI Configure Endpoint cmd sets up EP rings
Path A: driver already in the kernel
Path B: driver is an unloaded module
Bus walks unbound interfaces, runs the same
Builtins: hwdb, usb_id, input_id, path_id, net_id
xHC schedules transactions per endpoint type
Device returns DATA / ACK / NAK / STALL
TRBs on the endpoint's transfer ring,
Transfer Event TRB on the event ring + MSI-X
• Path A and Path B converge at probe(): A when the driver is built in or its module is already loaded; B when udev autoloads the module from MODALIAS.
• Every interface is matched separately, so one device can bind several drivers (e.g. usbhid on 1.0, cdc_acm on 1.1). Rows 6–8 repeat per interface; row 12 per subsystem device.
• Afterwards: runtime PM may autosuspend the idle device (USB suspend → U3). Unplug runs the reverse: port change → usb_disconnect() → yourdrv_disconnect() → KOBJ_REMOVE uevents.
• Inspect it live: udevadm monitor --kernel --udev --property · dmesg -w · lsusb -t · cat /sys/kernel/debug/usb/devices
